internal.title: Resolved: High Kafka Consumer Lag in Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 10:22 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for high Kafka consumer lag in the accounting service, with a backlog of approximately 5200 records. Initial diagnosis confirmed the backlog was causing processing delays. A proposed mitigation to enable a failure flag was blocked by guardrails. The team replanned and subsequently disabled the kafkaQueueProblems flag, which resolved the backlog and restored normal processing.

Key timeline:
- 10:22:04: Alert received for high Kafka consumer lag.
- 10:41:46: Diagnosis confirmed queue backlog.
- 10:41:51: Proposal to enable failure flag refused by guardrails.
- 10:42:10: Disabled kafkaQueueProblems flag.
- 10:42:10: Resolution approved and implemented.

The root cause was a processing backlog in Kafka consumer queues leading to delayed message handling. Recovery was achieved by disabling the problematic flag, which allowed the system to catch up.

Lessons learned include the importance of guardrails in preventing risky flag changes and the need for monitoring consumer lag metrics closely to detect backlogs early.

external.body: Between 10:22 and 10:42 UTC on 2026-11-08, the accounting service experienced processing delays due to a backlog in message consumption. This caused temporary delays in processing accounting data. The issue was identified and resolved within 20 minutes, and normal service has been restored. We continue to monitor the system to prevent recurrence.
